- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, particularly after recent spikes.
- Underestimate during mid-to-late horizon when true values show mean reversion toward prior levels.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 79.68 → 82.31) by overreacting to momentum.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; true values often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Forecast mean is consistently higher than true mean by 0.5–1.5 units across all horizons.
- Last 5–7 days of forecast often show overcorrection or premature normalization, missing true volatility.
- Model exhibits “sticky” bias toward recent high values, failing to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven corrections.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating volatility in the first 10 days, then underestimating in the last 10.
